articles.title: Rupee steady as oil firms buy dollars
articles.description: The Indian rupee showed minimal movement against the dollar on Friday, closing nearly unchanged. Oil companies actively bought dollars to restrict any considerable appreciation of the rupee. State-run banks also contributed to dollar selling in the market. The rupee fluctuated within a narrow scope, revealing a slightly negative trend, while Brent crude oil prices stabilized around eighty-three to eighty-four dollars per barrel.

articles.description: Upcoming inflation data poses a challenge to the stock market's recent technology-driven surge. Meanwhile, easing geopolitical concerns and dipping oil prices have provided some reprieve to investors. Strong corporate earnings are exceeding forecasts, fostering a positive outlook for stocks, while fluctuations in yields and oil prices are being meticulously observed.

articles.title: D-Street overcomes CAS pain to post weekly gains
articles.description: In a week marked by volatility, Indian equity indices ended on a positive note, showcasing their ability to bounce back. The initial worries prompted by the closing auction system quickly faded, as diminishing global oil prices and easing geopolitical conflicts uplifted investor sentiment. Mid and small-cap sectors demonstrated significant strength, with institutional investors, both domestic and foreign, snapping up Indian equities.
